text_blocks.speaker: Maury Povich
text_blocks.text: What was it that got you started into the Clipper investigation? Was it the money?

text_blocks.speaker: Pablo Torre
text_blocks.text: It was a tip, and it was a tip that I didn't fully understand when I first heard it. This was more than a year and a half ago. The tip was, you should look into this weird company called Aspire. They're a sponsor of the Clippers and Transmission. And I didn't really know what to do with that. But once Aspire went bankrupt and there was a bankruptcy filing, a document, and inside of that document you got to see that there was an LLC near the top of the list of creditors called KL2 Aspire LLC. And I happened to be a basketball fan and so I recognized, well okay, KL, that might be the initials of a certain player whose jersey number is two. KL2 Aspire, Aspire might be the name of this company. LLC, it raised the question of why in the hell is Kawhi Leonard's LLC getting paid, or rather, why were they owed outstanding $7 million?

The idea that you can be risk-seeking if you are being responsible and if you are telling the truth. If you are telling the truth, you can wear that as a suit of armor against the guy with billions upon billions of dollars.

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: Pablo Torre explains why he investigates billionaires
quotes.excerpt: There's an active federal investigation into Mark Walter, who happens to be also a man whose empire is built on insurance companies.

text_blocks.speaker: Maury Povich
text_blocks.text: You have a current investigation into a fellow named Mark Walter. Mark Walter happens to own the Los Angeles Dodgers and the Los Angeles basketball team.

text_blocks.speaker: Pablo Torre
text_blocks.text: There's an active federal investigation into Mark Walter, who happens to be also a man whose empire is built on insurance companies. And look, I am somebody who turns out hears something that sounds like straight up vegetables to a sports fan. You want to talk to me about insurance, life insurance and annuities now? And what I tell them is that what if it explained how a guy like Mark Walter came out of nowhere to afford the Los Angeles Dodgers, who paid the most money in the history of sports for a team at that time, on the back of an arranged deal that we reported on my show in which he started a local sports television channel and bought the team and figured out a way to borrow, according to our reporting, from a series of companies that he controlled that were premised on, according to the reporting, the premiums paid by America's parents and grandparents.

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: Pablo Torre explains his approach to investigative journalism
quotes.excerpt: I don't come at this from a position of, I want to destroy and burn down this world.

text_blocks.speaker: Pablo Torre
text_blocks.text: One of the things I've learned about these leagues, and I'm a huge, I should just say in case it's not obvious, I'm an enormous sports fan. I grew up like writing the stats of these players on the back of like little note cards, making my own version of like trading cards and stuff. I'm a sports nerd. I don't come at this from a position of, I want to destroy and burn down this world. I do not. But one of the things I've learned about leagues is that the question of due diligence is something we presume that they do. They do it, but the question of how how thorough is their investigation, repeatedly, I think there are real questions that are worth asking.
